summary: Iter4 verifies (a) the async caption pipeline (POST /projects/process now returns queued fast, background job runs, poll surfaces progress) and (b) native Whisper word timings via the versioned /llm/v1 proxy with timestamp_granularities=['word']. All 12 pytest cases in tests/test_iter4_async_flow.py PASS. Backend evidence: POST returned queued in 2.11s for an 8.2 MB toe-protector upload (target <30s); polling saw statuses queued/processing and labels 'Preparing audio'->'Listening word by word'->'Creating Roman Hinglish'->'Captions ready'; final project reached status=ready with 122+ words, unique durations >= 8, min duration 0.06s, monotonic starts, no zeros. Existing recovered projects match the RCA: project_f61fbdfdaeab (flying-beast) status=ready, 202 words, 30 unique durations, monotonic, last_end=64.64s vs duration 64.66s, no zero durations; project_81e50f2abf40 (toe protector) status=ready, 151 words, 23 unique durations, first_start=3.96s (correctly waits past silent intro), last_end=37.38s. ASS render generates one Dialogue event per word using each word's native start/end (regression: no 4-word phrase batching). server.py lifespan calls resume_pending_projects(db) before yield. Auth isolation: foreign user gets 404 on GET /projects/{id}. Frontend browser: registered user -> upload -> Generate -> progress panel visible immediately (label 'Uploading video' 2%, note 'You can keep this tab open...'), polls GET /projects/{id} every ~2.5s, label transitions through 'Upload complete', 'Listening word by word', 'Creating Roman Hinglish', editor opens after ~40s with full Hinglish transcript panel and timeline, 'Caption edits saved' toast after Save. One real Whisper+GPT budget respected (single POST on toe-protector-source.mp4). Skills loaded: ai-testing-core, ai-testing-audio, ai-testing-llm.

Screenshot /app/.screenshots/iter4_editor.png. skill: ai-testing-audio+llm

Preview shows only currently active word (structural) - pass - evidence: CaptionStudio.jsx line 27 - visibleWords = useMemo(() => activeIndex >= 0 ? [words[activeIndex]] : [], ...). Array is at most 1 element by construction. Live-playback observation of this in the UI was not possible because the video element could not stream (pre-existing /media Range issue reported below); the structural guarantee combined with the ASS-per-word test is sufficient proof of the fix.

minor.issue: Does not implement HTTP Range / 206 Partial Content. Returns HTTP 200 with full body for any Range header, and no Accept-Ranges response header. Chrome/Safari <video> elements need Range to progressively stream + seek MP4s whose moov atom is not at the front. Confirmed with `curl -H 'Range: bytes=0-524287'` returning HTTP 200 + full 8615126 bytes, no content-range. Pre-existing before iter4.

ui_bugs.issue: <video> element in the editor fails with MediaError code 4 (MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED) after both /media retries. In dev/preview builds this surfaces as a big red 'Uncaught runtime errors: The element has no supported sources' overlay. Root cause is the backend /media endpoint not supporting Range (see backend_issues.minor). onError retries once via mediaRetry but the second attempt also fails.

critical_code_review_comments: captions.project_media returns Response(data, media_type=content_type) - no Range handling, no Accept-Ranges header. For >~2MB videos this breaks HTML5 <video> playback in Chrome; use starlette.responses.StreamingResponse or a dedicated range responder (e.g. fastapi.responses.RangedFileResponse or a manual handler that reads the Range header and returns 206 with Content-Range/Accept-Ranges). This is the direct cause of the 'no supported sources' overlay.

caption_ai._transcription_pass mutates the singleton emergent_proxy_url every call (`stt.emergent_proxy_url = stt.emergent_proxy_url.rstrip('/') + '/v1'`). Because OpenAISpeechToText is re-instantiated per call this is fine today, but if the SDK ever memoises the URL between calls it will accumulate '/v1/v1/v1'. Consider computing the versioned URL once at import time or asserting `not endswith('/v1')` before appending.

caption_ai._normalize_word_timings floors end-start to 0.06s but keeps `start = max(word.start, previous_end)`. If Whisper returns overlapping words (which native whisper-1 can, esp. through a proxy), later words get pushed forward and drift can accumulate; adding a small tolerance (e.g. previous_end - 0.01) would preserve native starts better. Not seen in the two recovered projects but a latent bug on other clips.

captions.retranscribe_project sets status=queued and schedules a job WITHOUT clearing 'words' - a client polling immediately after Re-listen will still see the OLD word list until _run_caption_job's final update. Consider clearing words before scheduling so the UI doesn't briefly render stale captions on top of the 'Re-listen queued' state.

captions._run_caption_job stores project source_transcript AFTER Roman Hinglish conversion runs (progress 78% label 'Creating Roman Hinglish') but source_transcript is derived from the pre-conversion `words[].original`. This is correct, just worth documenting: source_transcript is set together with the final words update, not incrementally.

UploadStage.generate: catch block still shows toast.error(errorMessage(error)) even when error.response?.status === 402 case handles paywall - both branches run only one, good. But there is NO surface for backend 424/422/503 today - the toast will just print the FastAPI detail; acceptable for now.
CaptionStudio.relisten - same polling loop as UploadStage.generate; both use a fixed 2500ms interval that never backs off. Fine at current scale.

server.py lifespan awaits resume_pending_projects(db) synchronously before yielding, which means backend startup blocks while it enumerates queued/processing projects. Fine here (query is bounded to 100 rows and asyncio.create_task returns fast) but worth switching to asyncio.create_task(resume_pending_projects(db)) if the project count ever grows.

caption_ai.convert_to_hinglish: JSON extraction via `re.search(r'\[[\s\S]*\]', raw)` is greedy - if GPT ever emits stray brackets around the array this could grab extraneous text. Consider explicit json.loads with fallback to bracket search.
captions.py is now 288 lines - still under the 700-line threshold.
action_items: HIGH: Make GET /api/projects/{id}/media honour HTTP Range requests (return 206 Partial Content with Accept-Ranges: bytes and Content-Range headers). This will fix the 'Uncaught runtime errors: The element has no supported sources' overlay in the editor and unblock user testing of the preview video. See backend_issues.minor for the exact curl repro.
MEDIUM: In captions.retranscribe_project, clear the old `words` list when queuing Re-listen so the polling UI does not briefly render stale captions before the new transcript arrives.
LOW: In caption_ai._transcription_pass, guard against re-appending '/v1' if the SDK ever memoises stt.emergent_proxy_url between calls.
LOW: In UploadStage / CaptionStudio, consider a small backoff instead of a fixed 2500ms poll interval - fine at current scale but polite for many concurrent jobs.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter4 async pipeline + native timings fix is verified end-to-end. Backend regression: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview_url> python -m pytest tests/test_iter4_async_flow.py -v -n 0. Real-AI budget is ONE POST /projects/process + ONE POST /projects/{id}/retranscribe (~35-40s each on toe-protector-source.mp4). Unit-level tests (existing-Mongo checks, ASS render, resume-source-inspection) are free. If you need to also re-verify the exact 89.7MB / 64.66s flying-beast upload, keep in mind you would consume another Whisper pass; iter4 relied on the already-completed project_f61fbdfdaeab in Mongo (main agent's manual test) for that evidence. The pre-existing /media Range gap causes the 'Uncaught runtime errors: The element has no supported sources' overlay in the editor - this is NOT introduced by iter4 but IS a blocker for user preview playback; verify if main agent adds a 206 handler in the next iteration.
rca of the issue: Root causes (as documented by main agent E1 and confirmed here): (1) TIMING: the emergentintegrations default STT base URL (https://integrations.emergentagent.com/llm) returned words=null when both segment + word granularities were requested, so caption_ai used an equal-spacing fallback that scattered later words over the current segment and made the preview show 4 future words at once. Fix: caption_ai._transcription_pass now forces stt.emergent_proxy_url += '/v1' and asks only `timestamp_granularities=['word']`, receiving real Whisper native word timings; _normalize_word_timings floors zero-length edges to 0.06s without disturbing the native shape; CaptionStudio.visibleWords was narrowed to `[words[activeIndex]]`; _write_ass emits one Dialogue per word instead of a 4-word phrase batch. Evidence: 30 (flying-beast) and 23 (toe protector) unique word durations, no zeros, monotonic timing, toe first word starts at 3.96s (correctly past silent intro), long clip ends at 64.64s vs 64.66s duration. (2) LONG-VIDEO TIMEOUT: POST /projects/process did full Whisper + GPT + storage synchronously, so a 60-90s upload would exceed Cloudflare's ~100s cut and the backend would keep working after the client disconnected, occasionally creating duplicate projects. Fix: /projects/process now performs upload + object-storage put + Mongo insert, then schedules `_run_caption_job` via `asyncio.create_task` and returns queued in 2.11s (measured here). Background job progresses through 'Preparing audio' -> 'Listening word by word' -> 'Creating Roman Hinglish' -> 'Captions ready'. GET /projects/{id} exposes progress/processing_label for polling. server.py lifespan calls resume_pending_projects(db) to reschedule any queued/processing projects if the backend restarts mid-job. Retranscribe follows the same shape. Reproduction commands: pytest tests/test_iter4_async_flow.py::TestAsyncProjectProcess::test_process_returns_quickly_with_queued_status (POST speed), ::test_get_project_polling_progresses_to_ready (poll to ready), ::TestExistingNativeTimings (recovered project shape), ::TestAssPerWord (per-word ASS Dialogue). Mitigation status: FIXED end-to-end. Only remaining issue is the unrelated /media Range gap that blocks video preview playback in the editor.
